turns.text:
I’ll run the inverse design for the stated material ranges and check the resulting mix against the wall geometry, open time, and 28-day strength target.
The search found no mix that meets the printability and strength constraints together. Its leading candidates fail the physical wall check, so I’m checking a representative mix’s strength prediction and the nearest published evidence before giving a recommendation.
**No mix in the specified search space was verified to meet this print job.** The inverse design sampled 4,096 mixes and found none feasible under its printability and strength criteria.

A representative mix for **experimental screening**, expressed per unit binder mass, is:

| Component | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Portland cement / silica fume / limestone powder | 0.57 / 0.15 / 0.28 |
| Water / binder | 0.292 |
| Sand / binder | 1.21 |
| PCE / cellulose VMA | 0.82% / 0.19% of binder |

Its predicted 28-day compressive strength is **43.2 [26.7, 82.1] MPa**. The lower prediction bound falls below 30 MPa, so the strength requirement is not assured. Its predicted static yield stress is **734 [26, 5,620] Pa** and structuration rate is **0.483 [0.010, 18.442] Pa/s**. Treat these rheology estimates as order-of-magnitude guidance. As a measured strength analogue, a published OPC mortar with w/b 0.31 and s/b 1.20 reported 50.8 MPa at 28 days ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.addma.2020.101069)); that measurement does not establish this candidate’s printability.

The physical check classifies the candidate as **non-printable**: plastic collapse is expected around layer 6 of 48, and free-wall buckling around layer 11. At the specified speed, the layer cycle is 60 s. The model requires at least 430 s for stability, while the 60-minute open time permits at most 75 s per layer. At the current cycle, it estimates a required initial static yield stress of 9,313 Pa **or** a structuration rate of 3.462 Pa/s, with buckling still requiring attention. Slowing the print alone cannot close that time gap.

For a next trial, change the job or material constraints: brace the wall or add filaments to address buckling, and test measures that raise early yield stress and structuration, such as an accelerator, a revised VMA dose, or lower w/b. Measure fresh rheology, open time, print stability, and 28-day strength before adopting a mix.

Defaults used: 12.5 mm layer height, 29.61 mm layer width, zero dwell, moist curing, and a 50 mm cube strength comparison.
